tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing throughout ('Use this skill when...', 'Load it before answering...', 'Name every finding's...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms and intents (content/adversarial prompts getting through, PII exposure, off-topic/hallucinated answers, quota hits, intermittent blocking, latency) rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists many trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly ('even if no policy is named'), and while lengthy, remains a focused paragraph proportionate to the skill's complex domain.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a guardrail is configured but content, adversarial prompts or tool output still get through, sensitive data appears in prompts or completions or a model ignores redaction, answers are off-topic, hallucinated or blocked though correct, a guardrail limit or quota is hit...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what a guardrail is, what PII means) and instead jumps directly into domain-specific routing tables, check IDs, and AWS-specific API behaviors that an agent wouldn't know without this skill.
tests.evidence: 'Match the depth to the question.' and the Router table use dense, domain-specific shorthand rather than general explanations.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (API quirks, metric thresholds, service limits) is consistently pushed to references/ files and only summarized or pointed to in the body; the Router table and conditional branches link out rather than embedding detail.
tests.evidence: 'The exact read-only API calls and the field each contributes... are in references/collection-reference.md.'

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown links in the body (checks-guardrails.md, collection-reference.md, api-quirks.md, service-limits.md, documented-behavior.md, metrics-and-logs.md all appear as markdown links).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Reference links throughout the Router table and procedure steps specify precise conditions for loading each file, e.g., tied to specific symptoms or steps.
tests.evidence: 'PII in prompts or completions | `sensitiveInformationPolicy` entities... | references/checks-guardrails.md (LLM-GRD-003), references/api-quirks.md §17, §18'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use relative 'references/filename.md' format with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (account ID masking, read-only API guardrails, version-pinning checks) are highly prescriptive with exact rules, while flexible tasks (routing depth, answering from evidence) explain reasoning and allow judgment.
tests.evidence: 'Match the depth to the question.' combined with strict rule: 'Never call a mutating or invoking API... only this rule protects against them.'

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The Router table and procedure consistently designate a clear first action/default per scenario rather than presenting equal menus of options.
tests.evidence: 'Is anything protecting this model... | Enforcements (Step 1a), then ListGuardrails, then what each production path references'

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable review procedure (Steps 1-10) and router logic applicable to any guardrail/account, not a one-off instance; specific check-ids and templates are details within a reusable approach.
tests.evidence: 'Run these steps in order for each guardrail and each production invocation path in scope.'

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive 'Common wrong answers' section plus 'Error Handling' with api-quirks references that function as a gotchas section, documenting non-obvious pitfalls.
tests.evidence: '"InvocationsIntervened is zero, so the guardrail is healthy." Zero interventions and zero invocations look identical on that metric.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides a dedicated output template asset for its report-generating purpose.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline template exists in the body; the actual report template is stored in assets/ and only referenced.
tests.evidence: 'the output follows [the posture report template](assets/guardrail-posture-report-template.md), transcribed in full from any sub-agent output'

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is linked multiple times in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset reference specifies the condition for use (when a full report is requested/presented).
tests.evidence: 'When a full report is requested, the output follows [the posture report template](assets/guardrail-posture-report-template.md)'

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path format from skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N' labeling, matching the required format.
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: Enumerate guardrails with ListGuardrails...' through '- [ ] Step 10: Check blocked-message customization...'

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to re-check its findings, check-ids, masking, and scope before presenting.
tests.evidence: 'Before you present a result, re-check your own output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion.'
